attempts.record_raw: recorded/v1a1-check-1.stdout, recorded/v1a1-check-1.stderr (this label was already used by the merged 8-node probe, so the wrapper's duplicate-label guard wrote the -1 raw files; the log entry carries spec_sha256 05fffa36… for this spec)
attempts.note: tb, no rank pin. Engine ranked the worker BELOW the runtime (the return edge closes the cycle), so all four runtime endpoints crowded one rank gap and two labels landed nearer a neighbouring route. Rejected: 2 ambiguous label owners.
lr, no rank pin. The worker again ranked after the runtime, so the return edge looped back around the stacked callees: 2 crossings plus a skipped 'dispatches tasks' label. Rejected.

tb with rank pins [worker][runtime][engine,daemon] (the source's own flow direction: the worker produces task input, the runtime's callees sit below it) and label_slot on every edge. 0 crossings, all labels placed, no warning. SHIPPED (copied verbatim to specs/v1-seams.json, identical sha256).

views.carries: Task engine -> Container backend -> Task container, Task engine -> Filesystem + volumes -> Blobnet

attempts.note: tb. Mechanically clean, but the engine's two fan labels stacked in one left-hand band (rows 21-22 of the 77x47 dump), so neither label sits beside its own route. Rejected on readability, not on a check warning.

lr: each fan lane carries its label on its own row (starts/manages row 23, mount+snapshot row 31 of the 77x47 dump), 0 crossings. SHIPPED (copied verbatim to specs/v2-exec-storage.json, identical sha256).

lr with label_slot removed to force the honest proximity metric. The engine then reserved label room horizontally and the graph grew to 94 cells wide, i.e. it overflows the 77-column target ('graph overflows' banner in the pinned dump). Rejected: fit failure.

abandoned_shapes.note: Five ranks with label-driven rank gaps: 74 rows tall (overflows 47) and 2 ambiguous label owners in the runtime fan. Abandoned: no honest fit at the target size.

abandoned_shapes.shape: single merged view, label_slot on every edge
abandoned_shapes.note: Slots fixed the height (30 rows) but the fan labels still shared a band beside a neighbouring route: 2 ambiguous owners. Abandoned in favour of the two-view split.

abandoned_shapes.shape: two-node pair view (modal-worker, modal-runtime), lr, bare label placement
abandoned_shapes.note: The two pair lanes are 2 rows apart, so the first label took the row between them: exactly a tie with both routes. Abandoned (and it isolates the pair from the core, so the fan order would not be visible).

abandoned_shapes.shape: two-node pair view, lr, label_slot on both edges
abandoned_shapes.note: Both slots were reserved BELOW both lanes, so the two labels stack in one band two rows from either route. Measured evidence that a bare two-node pair gives the label machinery no side to separate on. Abandoned.

abandoned_shapes.note: minlen 2 opened a two-rank corridor, but the extent stayed 28 cells wide, so the 19-character label had no free cell at all. Abandoned.
